approachQuestion.prompt:
Finding a conflicting pair

Given n unsorted half-open bookings [start,end), return the original indices of ANY two bookings that overlap, or null if none do. Touching endpoints are not overlap; duplicate positive-length bookings do overlap. Input is immutable. Return a witness, not all conflicting pairs.

Input: bookings=[[8,10],[1,4],[4,7],[3,5]]
Output: [1,3]
Indices are zero-based; other genuine overlap witnesses are accepted.

Input: bookings=[[0,2],[2,4]]
Output: null

Constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; 0 ≤ start < end ≤ 1000000000. Use comparison-based ordering. Choose best worst-case time.

options.text: Copy indexed bookings and sort by start. Check each adjacent pair; return its original indices when the later start is strictly below the earlier end. Return null if no adjacent pair overlaps.
options.feedback: If no adjacent pair overlaps, each interval ends no later than the next start, so no nonadjacent pair can overlap either. One adjacent witness suffices; a full merged union is unnecessary.

options.text: Group by equal start and return two from any repeated-start group; otherwise return null.
options.feedback: For [[1,5],[3,7]], the starts differ but the bookings overlap. Equal starts are sufficient, not necessary.

options.text: Sort by start and return an adjacent pair when later.start ≤ earlier.end.
options.feedback: For [[0,2],[2,4]], equality only touches an excluded end. This produces a false witness instead of null.

options.text: Try every pair of original indices and return the first overlapping pair; return null if none overlaps.
options.feedback: This finds a valid witness or null, but absence of conflict forces checking all pairs. Ordering permits a single adjacent scan after sorting.

feedback.reason: Use adjacency as a certificate for existence of any overlap, while returning original-index evidence.
details: Copy bookings with original indices, sort by start using iterative bottom-up merge sort and a reusable buffer, then compare adjacent records until a witness is found or the list ends.

After sorting starts, any overlapping pair implies an overlapping adjacent pair: if an interval reaches a later start, it also reaches the intervening next start. Preserve original indices to return a witness in input identities.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For adjacent-start-witness, n is the booking count. Include the indexed copy and sort buffer; exclude the returned pair or null. Choose the tightest standard worst-case pair.
constraints: Analyze only the named method. Count all temporary arrays and the call stack; exclude the supplied input and returned output. Numeric comparisons, assignments and arithmetic take constant time, with no overflow.
No hashing or amortized data structure is used. All loops and binary searches are iterative; there is no recursive stack.

options.text: Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(n)
Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(1)

feedback.reason: Sorting dominates the adjacent witness scan even if a conflict is found early.
details: The sorting phase takes O(n log n), and the adjacent scan is at most linear. The indexed copy and reusable buffer use O(n); no overlap graph or recursive stack is created. Early witness discovery does not improve the worst-case sorting cost.
Comparison ordering by iterative merge sort; original-index witness.
“Time O(n), auxiliary space O(1)”: An adjacent scan is linear only after sorting. This implementation also creates indexed copies and a merge buffer.
“Time O(n²), auxiliary space O(n)”: Pair enumeration is not performed. After sorting, only neighboring records are tested.
“Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(1)”: The copy preserving original indices and reusable sorting buffer are auxiliary arrays and cannot be excluded with the returned witness.
